samples: This program is a command-line tool that joins its arguments into one question, sends it with the API key from the `CHAT_API_KEY` environment variable to a chat-completion service, and prints the text of the first answer. It uses a placeholder web address and a placeholder model name, so you would have to change both for a real service. It fails with a clear error if the key is missing, the reply has no answers, or the network or JSON handling goes wrong, and it needs console, environment and HTTP permissions. One caution: the HTTP call it makes (a plain `post`) is not in the standard library as I know it, which lists only `post_json`, so it may not pass the checker as written.

This command-line tool joins its arguments into one question, sends it with the API key from the `CHAT_API_KEY` environment variable to a chat-completion web service, and prints the text of the first answer. It stops with a distinct error if the key is missing, the reply has no answers, or the HTTP call or response parsing fails, and it includes an offline test that replays a recorded exchange. Before relying on it, note that the web address and model name are placeholders you would need to replace, and that it asks for unrestricted network access rather than limiting it to one host. It also calls an HTTP post function whose name differs from the one in the language's documented library (`post_json`), so check that this compiles.

This is a small command-line tool that joins the command-line arguments into one question, reads an API key from the `CHAT_API_KEY` environment variable, sends the question to a chat-completions web service, and prints the text of the first answer. It stops with a distinct error if the key is missing, the reply has no answers, or the network or JSON handling fails, and it has one offline test that replays a recorded response. One caution: it relies on an HTTP post function that is not in the library list I know of (only `post_json` is), so confirm it compiles before depending on it, and note that your question and API key are sent to the hard-coded example endpoint.

This command-line program joins its arguments into one question, reads an API key from the `CHAT_API_KEY` environment variable, sends the question to a chat-completion web service over HTTP, and prints the text of the first answer. If the key is missing, the reply has no answers, or the HTTP or JSON step fails, it stops with a descriptive error instead of printing anything, and it includes an offline test that replays a recorded response. Before relying on it, note that the endpoint and model name are placeholders, and the HTTP call uses a function named `post`, while the library lists only `post_json`, so it may not pass the checker without a fix.

This is a command-line tool that takes your question from the program arguments and your API key from the `CHAT_API_KEY` environment variable, sends the question to a chat-completions web service, and prints the text of the first answer. It needs console, environment and network access, and it fails with a clear error if the key is missing, the reply has no answers, or the request or response handling goes wrong. Before relying on it, note that the endpoint address and model name are placeholders you would have to replace, and the HTTP call it uses is not among the std.http functions the cheat sheet lists (`get` and `post_json`), so it may not compile as written.
